sprint_note: Adds a read-only, additive-only review-performance statistics endpoint and page: three rolling trailing windows (day/week/month) aggregated from the existing essaycards.review_events table, scheduler-agnostic, no schema change.
summary: Adds GET /api/essaycards/review-stats/summary and a Stats page reporting how the reviewer performed over the last day, week, and month, aggregated across every essay and both schedulers from the existing review_events history.

classification.why_application: The three window definitions, the grade-breakdown vocabulary (again/hard/good/easy, recall_rate, failures), and the choice to aggregate across schedulers rather than per-scheduler are EssayCards-specific interpretations of its own review history (CLAUDE.md glossary) — a 'how did I do' report meaningful only in terms of this app's due-queue/session model, not a reusable technical capability.
non_goals: Historical trend charts or graphs over time
Calendar-aligned 'today'/'this week' boundaries (as opposed to the rolling windows this sprint uses)
Any change to essaycards.review_events, backend/routers/experiment.py, or GET /flashcards/stats
Any write/mutation endpoint — this entire sprint is read-only
classification.not_platform: This is a narrow, app-specific rollup of one application's own append-only review log, using vocabulary (grade, recall_rate, failures, established/learning thresholds by convention elsewhere in the app) that has no meaning outside EssayCards. It is not exposed to, or reusable by, any other Atlas application.

consumes: essaycards.review_events (Sprint10, append-only) — read-only, no schema change; columns used: reviewed_at, grade, flashcard_id, prior_review_interval is NOT used as a filter this sprint (see invariants)
Postgres now() — sole time authority (R-CON-AL-06); no client-supplied time input anywhere in this feature
platform_errorhandling — existing exception handlers / request timing, unchanged
provides: GET /api/essaycards/review-stats/summary — Dataset, always exactly three rows (day, week, month, in that fixed order)
invariants: Windows are rolling and off Postgres now(), computed fresh on every request, matching the existing rolling-window convention already established elsewhere in this app (GET /flashcards/due's RECENT window, GET /flashcards/stats' forecast bands): day = reviewed_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'; week = reviewed_at >= now() - interval '7 days'; month = reviewed_at >= now() - interval '30 days'.

The three windows are independent and overlapping, not a partition — a review counted in day is also counted in week and month. This is the opposite shape from GET /flashcards/stats' seven non-overlapping zero-filled bands, and that difference is intentional (see classification.non_goals and 00_draft.md §1).
The response always has exactly three rows in the fixed order day, then week, then month — a window with zero reviews still appears, zero-filled in every count column, never omitted.

recall_rate = (reviews - failures) / reviews, and is null (never 0) when reviews == 0 for that window — the same 'no data yet vs. 0% recall' distinction already established in backend/routers/experiment.py. recall_rate must never be rendered or computed without its reviews count read together (R-CON-BP-08 self-containment).

failures is always exactly equal to again_count — named separately only because recall_rate is derived from it and the two must always be read together, mirroring GET /experiment/summary's identical convention.
again_count + hard_count + good_count + easy_count always sums to reviews for the same window row.
unique_cards = count(distinct flashcard_id) within the window; may be less than reviews when a card was reviewed more than once inside the same window.

The aggregation is scheduler-agnostic by construction: no query in this feature groups by, filters on, or otherwise reads essaycards.review_events.scheduler. This is deliberately a different, complementary report to GET /experiment/summary (Classic vs FSRS comparison) — a reviewer performance rollup, not an algorithm comparison. Do not add a scheduler column or a per-scheduler variant to this endpoint; that already exists at /experiment/summary.

Unlike GET /experiment/summary's ordinary_due_reviews filter (prior_review_interval >= interval '24 hours'), this endpoint applies no prior_review_interval filter — every completed review in the window counts, including relearning/rapid retries, because this page reports the reviewer's actual completed work in the window, not isolated evidence of long-term retention.
No query parameters this sprint (R-CON-AL-01) — the endpoint takes no input beyond the implicit request; every allowed 'combination' is the single no-parameter case, trivially closed (R-CON-AL-02).

All three window rows are computed by exactly one SQL query against essaycards.review_events using count(*) filter (where ...) / count(distinct ...) filter (where ...) expressions per window and per grade, mirroring the filter (where ...) style already used in backend/routers/experiment.py's _review_counts_by_scheduler — never three separate round trips.
failure_modes: Unexpected DB/query failure surfaces as ApiError (500) via the existing platform_errorhandling exception handlers, installed unchanged in backend/main.py — there is no endpoint-specific validation failure mode, since the endpoint accepts no parameters.

provides: backend.routers.review_stats — a new router (prefix /review-stats) included by main.py after the existing seven routers (essays/flashcards/exploration/examinations/images/nuggets/experiment)

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/essaycards/review-stats/summary
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Review-performance dashboard data source: how the reviewer did over the trailing day/week/month, aggregated across every essay and both schedulers.

query_behavior.allowed_combinations: n/a — the single no-parameter request is the only allowed call shape
query_behavior.ordering: fixed: day row, then week row, then month row — always exactly these three, in this order
query_behavior.grouping: one row per rolling window (day/week/month); no scheduler/essay/topic grouping this sprint
query_behavior.time_basis: server time only — Postgres now(), read fresh on every request (R-CON-AL-06); no client-supplied time anywhere in this feature
query_behavior.boundary_construction: day: reviewed_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'; week: reviewed_at >= now() - interval '7 days'; month: reviewed_at >= now() - interval '30 days'; windows are independent/overlapping, not exclusive bands
query_behavior.empty_result_behavior: not applicable to the row set (always exactly 3 rows); a window with zero reviews still appears with reviews=0, unique_cards=0, all four grade counts=0, failures=0, recall_rate=null
query_behavior.zero_fill_behavior: always exactly 3 rows in fixed order; every count column zero-fills when a window has no reviews; recall_rate is null (not 0) in that case, never conflated with a real 0% recall rate
query_behavior.row_shape: period (string: 'day' | 'week' | 'month'), reviews (number), unique_cards (number), again_count (number), hard_count (number), good_count (number), easy_count (number), failures (number, always equal to again_count), recall_rate (number 0..1, nullable)

internal_flow.name: review_stats_aggregate_query
internal_flow.description: get_review_stats_summary (backend/routers/review_stats.py) runs one SQL statement against essaycards.review_events, outer-restricted by WHERE reviewed_at >= now() - interval '30 days' (the widest of the three windows; day and week are subsets, so this bound never excludes a row any window needs while avoiding a full-table scan). For each window w in (day: 24 hours, week: 7 days, month: 30 days) it computes count(*) filter (where reviewed_at >= now() - interval '<w>') as <w>_reviews, count(distinct flashcard_id) filter (where reviewed_at >= now() - interval '<w>') as <w>_unique_cards, and count(*) filter (where reviewed_at >= now() - interval '<w>' and grade = '<g>') as <w>_<g>_count for each grade g in (again, hard, good, easy) — one row of 3*(2+4)=18 scalar aggregates returned.
outputs: single aggregate row dict keyed by <window>_<metric>

internal_flow.name: build_summary_rows
internal_flow.description: Python-side: for period in ('day', 'week', 'month'), in that fixed order, read the aggregate row's <period>_reviews/<period>_unique_cards/<period>_<grade>_count columns; failures = again_count; recall_rate = (reviews - failures) / reviews if reviews > 0 else None. Builds exactly 3 row dicts in fixed order — no coalescing against a fixed label list is needed (unlike GET /experiment/summary's per-scheduler GROUP BY), because the single aggregate query already returns one row covering all three windows regardless of whether any reviews exist.
outputs: list of exactly 3 row dicts, period='day' then 'week' then 'month'

internal_flow.name: review_stats_dataset_response
internal_flow.description: Wraps the 3 rows in Dataset(meta=DatasetMeta(object_type='review_stats_summary', label='Review Stats Summary', total=3, page=1, page_size=3, row_actions=[]), schema=REVIEW_STATS_SUMMARY_SCHEMA, rows=rows), returned via the same _dataset_response(dataset) -> JSONResponse pattern used by backend/routers/experiment.py.

internal_flow.name: review_stats_view_fetch_render
internal_flow.description: ReviewStatsView (src/ShellEntry.tsx) fetches GET /essaycards/review-stats/summary once on mount via the existing apiFetch<Dataset<T>>/isApiError/ErrorCard/Skeleton convention (same as ExperimentDashboardView). Renders three cards/columns in the fixed row order (Day, Week, Month), each showing its reviews count, recall_rate as a rounded percentage or the literal string 'No reviews yet' when recall_rate is null (never '0%' for that case), and the four-grade breakdown (again/hard/good/easy counts). Reuses existing Material 3 surface tokens (var(--md-sys-color-surface-variant) etc.) already used by ExperimentDashboardView/ReviewStatsPanel — no new visual tokens introduced.

internal_flow.name: stats_nav_registration
internal_flow.description: src/shellConfig.ts gains a nav entry {id: 'essaycards-stats', label: 'Stats', path: '/essaycards/stats', order: 5} in both mobilePrimaryNav and desktopNav, immediately after the existing essaycards-experiment entry (order: 4) — same registration mechanism already used for every other top-level EssayCards view, no new nav pattern. src/ShellEntry.tsx's Routes gains <Route path="/stats" element={<ReviewStatsView />} />.
outputs: Stats entry visible in both nav surfaces; /essaycards/stats resolves to ReviewStatsView

deferred_decisions: Whether a future sprint should add per-essay/topic scoping or a per-scheduler breakdown to this page (explicitly out of scope this sprint per non_goals).

risks.risk: essaycards.review_events has no index with reviewed_at as a leading column (existing indexes are (flashcard_id, reviewed_at desc) and (scheduler, prior_review_interval)); the outer WHERE reviewed_at >= now() - interval '30 days' restriction in step 1 cannot use an index scan and falls back to a sequential scan bounded only by table size, not by the 30-day window.
risks.impact: Acceptable at current review_events volume; if row count grows significantly (Sprint10's own deferred_decisions already flags review_events' unbounded append-only growth), this endpoint's latency will degrade before an index on reviewed_at is added — a future-sprint indexing follow-up, not a defect in this design.

open_questions.question: Should essaycards.review_events eventually get an index on reviewed_at (or (reviewed_at) alone) once its row count/latency profile is measured against this endpoint?
